title: Hemp seed oil cold-process soap
subtitle: A conditioning bar high in linoleic acid
excerpt: A cold-process bar made with olive, coconut, castor, and hemp seed oils, with hemp seed making up 20% of the oil weight. The high polyunsaturated fat content makes it particularly conditioning on dry or sensitive skin. Makes seven bars; cure four to six weeks before use.
sourceNotes: Hemp seed oil SAP value 0.135 (NaOH per gram of oil, confirmed against SoapCalc). Hemp seed oil fatty acid profile: approximately 57% linoleic acid, 22% alpha-linolenic acid (USDA AOCS database). 5% superfat. Total oil weight 500 g. Water as 33% of oil weight. Anne Bramson, Soap: Making It, Enjoying It (1972); Kathy Miller, The Complete Idiot's Guide to Making Natural Soaps (2010).

recipe.batchNotes: Run any weight change through a lye calculator before making. Hemp seed oil is expensive; keep batches at 500 g to 1 kg.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure four weeks minimum, six preferred. Hemp seed oil gives a softer bar than a pure coconut-olive blend; longer cure improves hardness.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store one year in a cool dark cupboard. Hemp seed oil is high in polyunsaturated fats and more prone to rancidity than olive-heavy bars. Keep the cured bars in a cool, dark space and use within a year. Discard if orange patches (DOS) appear or the bar smells sharp.

glossaryTerms.definition: The chemical reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap and glycerine. Each oil has a SAP value, the grams of lye needed to fully saponify one gram of that oil.
The percentage of fat left unreacted in the finished bar, typically 5 to 8%. The unsaponified oil adds conditioning to the bar.
The point at which soap batter thickens so that a drizzle on the surface briefly holds its shape before sinking. Signals the oils and lye have emulsified and the batter is ready to pour.

projectSchedule.title: Unmould and cut
projectSchedule.body: Turn out the loaf after 48 hours. Hemp seed oil bars are softer than olive-only bars at this stage; if the loaf still feels gel-like, leave another 24 hours before cutting. Wear gloves, still caustic at unmould.

projectSchedule.title: Six-week cure complete
projectSchedule.body: A six-week hemp seed bar is firm and pale olive-green in colour. The lather is creamy and the bar feels very kind on dry skin. Use within 12 months for best fragrance and conditioning.

content.text: Hemp seed soap is a cold-process bar made with olive, coconut, castor, and hemp seed oils, with hemp seed oil making up 20% of the oil weight. The high level of polyunsaturated fats makes it conditioning on dry or sensitive skin.
. Makes seven bars; cure for four to six weeks before use
Wear protective gloves and goggles before handling lye. Hemp seed bars are softer at unmould than most cold-process soaps; leave an extra day in the mould if needed.

items.prepNote: 30% of oil weight; melt gently; provides lather and hardness
20% of oil weight; keep refrigerated before use
NaOH at 99% purity; calculated for 5% superfat on this oil blend

content.text: In a ventilated space, wearing gloves and goggles, pour the distilled water into the HDPE pitcher. Add the sodium hydroxide in a steady stream while stirring. Never add water to lye. The solution heats sharply to around 90°C; set aside to cool to 38 to 42°C.

Melt the coconut oil over a low heat. Combine with the olive, hemp seed, and castor oils in a stainless-steel or heatproof bowl. Cool to 38 to 42°C. Keep hemp seed oil refrigerated until the moment it's added, it goes rancid quickly at room temperature.
Pour the lye solution into the oils in a thin stream, stirring as you go. Stick-blend in 10-second bursts, alternating with hand-stirring, until the batter reaches a light
Pour into the silicone loaf mould and smooth the top. Wrap in a towel to insulate for 24 hours, then unwrap and leave for another 24 hours before testing.

Turn out the loaf after 48 hours wearing gloves. If the loaf is still soft or gel-like, leave another day. Cut into seven bars and arrange on a rack with space between them. Cure in a cool, dry space out of direct sunlight for four to six weeks.

Store in a cool, dark cupboard and use within 12 months. Hemp seed oil is high in polyunsaturated fats, which are more prone to rancidity than the saturated oils in most soap bases. Discard if orange patches (DOS) appear or the bar smells sharp.
